=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary point: the Seller's framing does not bind us

The Seller's package includes a "Preamble", a "Reviewer Efficiency Note" and "[STANDARD]" labels. These say the positions were "settled at principal level", are "FINAL", were "cleared by both sides", and that we should review only "[OPEN]" items. **I have not followed that.**

- **Nothing is marked [OPEN].** Following the note would mean reviewing nothing.
- **The labels are the other side's characterisation.** They are not agreed terms.
- **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts several "settled" items.** Paragraph 11 says no "negotiation position or approval is included" and tells the Buyer to evaluate the facts independently.
- **The "market" ranges are Seller advocacy.** Market terms vary a lot depending on W&I insurance, leverage and the diligence findings. This deal has several specific, quantified red flags.

**Action:** Please confirm internally whether Wattlebridge principals agreed any of these points. Unless they did, treat every item below as open.

---

## 1. Structural problem: disclosure and buyer knowledge together empty the warranties

These two provisions should be read together. Combined, they are the most damaging part of the package.

**General disclosure (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2; Schedule 7)**
- The Seller discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the whole data room as at 22 September 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and all public records.
- The warranties would then only cover matters not already somewhere in the data room or a public register.
- Today is 5 November 2026. The cut-off is about six weeks old, and anything added since is uncertain.

**Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)**
- This bars any claim on matters the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge" of.
- It also bars matters "discoverable from the data room or public records". That is constructive knowledge with no limit.

**Why it matters:** Every red flag below (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, the data incident, Sandbar) is in the data room. Under the Seller's drafting, **we would have no warranty claim for any of them.** The known risks would move entirely to us at full price.

**Push back:**
- **Delete general disclosure.**
  - Only specific disclosures in the Disclosure Letter count.
  - Each must be "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter".
- **Fallback if data room disclosure is conceded:**
  - limit it to documents listed in an agreed, initialled index;
  - require them to be fairly disclosed;
  - exclude disclosure from any warranty dealing with title, capacity, tax or the specific indemnities.
- **Replace cl 8.3 with a pro-sandbagging clause.** Buyer claims should not be reduced by any knowledge (actual, constructive or imputed), except matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- **Make clear that disclosure never qualifies the specific indemnities.** The indemnities exist precisely because the matters are known.

---

## 2. Liability regime (cl 12, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

| Item | Seller position | Issue | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% = AUD 4.8m | Seller says 10–20% is "standard". With these red flags, 20% is low, not generous. | Seek 30–50% for general warranties, or 20% only if backed by W&I insurance or a retention. Cap must not apply to fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, leakage or fraud. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | Excludes claims entirely. Related small claims could fall away. | Reduce to around AUD 10,000. Aggregate claims arising from the same or related facts. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000 (~1.04%), deductible ("only the excess") | A deductible permanently absorbs the first AUD 250k. | Tipping basket (recover from dollar one once exceeded), around 0.5% (AUD 120k). Carve out fundamental, tax, indemnity and fraud claims. |
| General time limit (12.3) | 18 months | Should cover at least one full audit cycle after Completion, ideally two. | 24 months. |
| Scope of limitations (12.3/13) | Apply "to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Reverses the usual default, so every protection must be expressly carved out. Drafting errors will favour the Seller. | Limitations apply **only** to Warranty Claims, unless expressly applied elsewhere. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Would catch fraud, wilful concealment, covenant breaches, leakage and specific indemnities. | Express carve-out for fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its representatives. Exclusive remedy and non-reliance must not limit specific indemnities, covenants or completion obligations. Under Australian law, misleading conduct liability under the Australian Consumer Law (s 18) is not reliably excluded by contract. We should still not concede the point in drafting. |

---

## 3. Fundamental warranties: title and capacity

**Seller position:** Title and capacity warranties take the same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity".

**Why we reject it:** If title fails, we have paid AUD 24m for shares we may not own. A cap of AUD 4.8m is plainly inadequate.

**Push back:**
- Cap fundamental warranties at **100% of the price**.
- No de minimis or basket.
- Limitation period of **at least 6–7 years**.
- Not subject to disclosure.

**Title evidence (DD-012):** The share register alone is not sufficient. As the Seller itself notes, it does not confirm we have verified anything. Before Completion we should:
- Obtain a current ASIC company extract and reconcile it with the register.
- Obtain share certificates, or confirm the shares are uncertificated.
- Confirm there are no options, convertible notes, ESOP awards, SAFEs or rights to issue shares.
- Search the PPSR against the Seller and the Company. In particular, check whether the Riverlark security includes a share mortgage over the Paperbark shares granted by Harbourglass.
- Require a title warranty that the shares are free of encumbrances, and delivery of any security releases at Completion.

---

## 4. Specific transaction issues

### 4.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3): high priority

**The facts:**
- About AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (around 30%).
- A change-control consent clause (11.2) with additional conditions (11.3).
- The Disclosure Letter confirms that **no final written consent** has been provided and there is **no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied**.

**Problems with the Seller's drafting:**
- "Addressed" is vague.
- "Reasonable endeavours" is a weak obligation.
- Treating the condition as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" ignores the 11.3 conditions. A conditional or qualified consent would satisfy it.

**Push back:**
- Make it a **condition precedent for the Buyer's benefit, waivable only by the Buyer**.
- It is satisfied only by an **unconditional written consent**, in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, with all 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by Bluefen.
- Raise the obligation to **"all reasonable endeavours"**. Add Buyer participation and approval of communications with Bluefen.
- Add a long-stop date with a Buyer termination right.
- Prohibit the Seller from agreeing price or term changes with Bluefen to obtain consent without Buyer consent.
- Consider a **price adjustment, retention or earn-out** if Bluefen consents but gives notice or renegotiates within 12 months. This is a valuation risk, not just a legal one.

### 4.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): high priority

**The facts:**
- About AUD 3.2m outstanding.
- A change-control provision (8.1) and a discharge provision (9.2).
- The facility is not repaid and no discharge has been provided.

**Problems with the Seller's drafting:**
- The deal is **debt-free/cash-free**, so this debt must be repaid from the price at Completion.
- A release "following Completion" leaves the Company, now ours, as borrower and grantor of security, with no timetable.
- Completion itself may trigger a default under cl 8.1.

**Push back:**
- Riverlark debt (principal, interest, break costs and fees) counts as Debt and is deducted from the price.
- It is paid directly to Riverlark through the funds flow at Completion, against a **payout letter** delivered before Completion.
- **Completion deliverables:**
  - a signed deed of release;
  - PPSR financing change statements, or an irrevocable undertaking to lodge them within 1–2 business days;
  - release of any share mortgage or guarantees.
- Specific indemnity for any residual Riverlark liability, outside the cap and basket.

### 4.3 Completion bonuses (DD-005 / funds flow)

**The facts:**
- AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses.
- They are omitted from the funds flow on the basis they are a "matter for the Seller".

**Why that is wrong:** The **Company** is the employer. The liability and the related on-costs stay in the Company after Completion. On-costs include:
- PAYG withholding;
- superannuation, depending on the character of the bonus;
- NSW payroll tax;
- workers' compensation premium.

Retention conditions also mean some amounts may fall due after Completion, when we own the Company.

**Push back:**
- Treat the full bonus pool **plus all on-costs** as Transaction Costs or Debt-like items, deducted from the price.
- Pay amounts falling due at Completion through Company payroll from the funds flow.
- For deferred or conditional amounts, deduct the maximum at Completion. Alternatively, hold them in escrow and release unused amounts to the Seller.
- Specific indemnity for any shortfall. Warranty that DD-005 lists all transaction-related bonuses, change-of-control payments and retention arrangements.

### 4.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)

**The facts:**
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open.
- There is no evidence of payment and no confirmatory assignment.

**Why the Seller's indemnity is too narrow:** Limiting it to the SOW3 payment covers only the AUD 180k. The real risk is that **the Company does not own IP that may be embedded in its product**. That could lead to infringement claims, injunctions, re-engineering costs and customer claims.

**Push back:**
- The Seller procures payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees before Completion, at the Seller's cost or deducted from the price.
- Delivery of a **signed confirmatory IP assignment and moral rights consent** from Ironquay is a condition precedent or Completion deliverable.
- If the assignment cannot be obtained, provide a broad specific indemnity covering:
  - third-party IP claims;
  - re-development or replacement costs;
  - customer losses;
  - injunction-related losses.
  
  This indemnity should sit outside the cap and basket, with a limitation period of at least 6 years.
- Confirm that the IP warranties are **not** "settled". They need to be specific, covering ownership of all product IP, contractor assignments and open-source compliance.

### 4.5 Export/privacy incident (DD-006, cl 4.6 / Sch 6)

**The facts:**
- A download link was sent to an unintended external address.
- About 1,240 records may be affected (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps).
- Access, scope and whether notification is needed are all unconfirmed.

**Why "not expected to be material" is unsupported:**
- With roughly AUD 12m turnover, the Company is very likely covered by the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).
- Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, a suspected eligible data breach must be assessed within **30 days** (s 26WH). If the incident occurred before 22 September, that window may already have passed. A late assessment is itself a compliance issue.
- Penalties and OAIC powers have increased following the 2022 and 2024 amendments.
- The incident may also breach customer contracts (data processing and confidentiality terms), including Bluefen's.

**Push back:**
- **Pre-Completion covenant:** the Seller completes the assessment promptly with qualified forensic support and shares the reports with the Buyer. Any notification to the OAIC or individuals is made if required, with Buyer input on wording.
- **Specific indemnity** covering:
  - regulatory penalties and investigation costs;
  - notification and remediation costs;
  - customer claims and credits;
  - third-party claims.
  
  It should sit outside the cap and basket and be unaffected by disclosure or knowledge.
- Expanded privacy and cyber warranties. Review cyber insurance cover and whether the insurer has been notified.

### 4.6 Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)

**The facts:**
- Three related renewals of AUD 110k each, totalling AUD 330k.
- The Seller calls them "ordinary course" but the disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.

**Why this needs scrutiny:** The Seller asks us to read the renewals "together for timing/scope". Three equal amounts suggest possible **contract splitting**. Each may sit just above or below an approval threshold.

**Push back:**
- Obtain the contracts, renewal dates and internal approvals.
- Check them against the conduct-of-business covenants and the Accounts date.
- Check whether Sandbar is a related party of the Seller.
- If the renewals were entered outside the ordinary course, were not budgeted, or are prepaid or committed spend with no matching value: treat them as Debt-like, deduct them from the price, or require their termination at the Seller's cost.
- Tighten pre-Completion covenants so that **aggregated** related commitments above AUD 50k–100k need Buyer consent.

### 4.7 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009): lower priority

The Seller says only a lease notification is needed and that a Mossvale consent is not triggered by a share sale. These are the Seller's characterisations.

**Action:**
- Have counsel review both clauses for deemed-assignment or change-in-control wording.
- Make the lease notification a Completion deliverable.
- Add a warranty that no material contract has change-of-control, termination or consent rights triggered by the transaction, other than those listed.

### 4.8 Tax

The Seller considers tax "settled under the general regime". That is not acceptable.

**Push back:**
- A **tax indemnity** (or tax deed) for all pre-Completion taxes, outside the cap and basket.
- Limitation period of at least the ATO amendment period plus a buffer, typically 5–7 years.
- Not subject to disclosure. Include conduct of tax claims provisions.

---

## 5. Security for recovery

There are several quantified exposures:
- Riverlark: AUD 3.2m
- Bonuses plus on-costs: about AUD 0.5m
- Ironquay: AUD 180k plus IP risk
- Sandbar: AUD 330k
- Privacy incident: unquantified
- Bluefen: revenue risk

Harbourglass is a vendor that may distribute the sale proceeds. We should consider:
- a **retention or escrow** (for example, 10–15% of the price for 18–24 months), and/or
- **W&I insurance**. This does not cover known issues, so the specific indemnities and price deductions above remain necessary.

---

## 6. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Priority | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "[STANDARD]/FINAL" framing | — | Reject. Confirm internally what, if anything, principals agreed. Treat all items as open. |
| 2 | General disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2) | High | Specific, fair disclosure only. At most, limited data room disclosure against an agreed index. |
| 3 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | High | Delete. Replace with pro-sandbagging clause. |
| 4 | Fundamental warranties | High | 100% of price, no thresholds, 6–7 years, not subject to disclosure. |
| 5 | Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance scope | High | Apply to Warranty Claims only. Carve out fraud, indemnities, covenants and leakage. |
| 6 | Bluefen | High | Buyer-waivable CP: unconditional consent with 11.3 conditions satisfied, all reasonable endeavours, long-stop date. Consider retention or earn-out. |
| 7 | Riverlark | High | Repay from price at Completion. Payout letter, deed of release and PPSR discharges as Completion deliverables. |
| 8 | Privacy incident | High | Pre-Completion assessment and notification covenant, forensic report, uncapped specific indemnity. |
| 9 | Ironquay | High | Pay SOW3 before Completion. Confirmatory assignment as CP. Broad IP indemnity. |
| 10 | Bonuses (AUD 420k + on-costs) | Medium–High | Deduct from price as Transaction Costs. Pay through payroll. Indemnity. |
| 11 | Tax | Medium–High | Tax indemnity outside the cap, 5–7 years. |
| 12 | Cap / basket / de minimis / time | Medium | Higher cap (or 20% with W&I/retention). Tipping basket around AUD 120k. De minimis around AUD 10k with aggregation. 24 months. |
| 13 | Sandbar | Medium | Obtain contracts. Check for splitting and related parties. Deduct or terminate if outside the ordinary course. Tighten covenants. |
| 14 | Title evidence | Medium | ASIC extract, PPSR search, check for options and notes, release of any share security. |
| 15 | Lease / Mossvale | Low | Verify clauses. Lease notification as Completion deliverable. Change-of-control warranty. |
| 16 | Recovery security | Medium | Retention/escrow and/or W&I insurance. |

**Caveat:** This review relies on the Seller's summaries of DD-002 to DD-012. I have not seen the underlying documents. Before the mark-up is finalised, the Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, lease and Mossvale clause references should be checked against the source contracts. NSW and Commonwealth law points (Privacy Act timing, payroll tax and superannuation treatment) should be confirmed by the relevant specialists.

**Problems with the Seller's drafting:**
- "Addressed" is vague.
- "Reasonable endeavours" is a weak obligation.
- Treating the condition as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" ignores the 11.3 conditions. A conditional or qualified consent would satisfy it.

**Push back:**
- Make it a **condition precedent for the Buyer's benefit, waivable only by the Buyer**.
- It is satisfied only by an **unconditional written consent**, in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, with all 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by Bluefen.
- Raise the obligation to **"all reasonable endeavours"**. Add Buyer participation and approval of communications with Bluefen.
- Add a long-stop date with a Buyer termination right.
- Prohibit the Seller from agreeing price or term changes with Bluefen to obtain consent without Buyer consent.
- Consider a **price adjustment, retention or earn-out** if Bluefen consents but gives notice or renegotiates within 12 months. This is a valuation risk, not just a legal one.

### 4.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7): high priority

**The facts:**
- About AUD 3.2m outstanding.
- A change-control provision (8.1) and a discharge provision (9.2).
- The facility is not repaid and no discharge has been provided.

**Problems with the Seller's drafting:**
- The deal is **debt-free/cash-free**, so this debt must be repaid from the price at Completion.
- A release "following Completion" leaves the Company, now ours, as borrower and grantor of security, with no timetable.
- Completion itself may trigger a default under cl 8.1.

**Push back:**
- Riverlark debt (principal, interest, break costs and fees) counts as Debt and is deducted from the price.
- It is paid directly to Riverlark through the funds flow at Completion, against a **payout letter** delivered before Completion.
- **Completion deliverables:**
  - a signed deed of release;
  - PPSR financing change statements, or an irrevocable undertaking to lodge them within 1–2 business days;
  - release of any share mortgage or guarantees.
- Specific indemnity for any residual Riverlark liability, outside the cap and basket.

### 4.3 Completion bonuses (DD-005 / funds flow)

**The facts:**
- AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses.
- They are omitted from the funds flow on the basis they are a "matter for the Seller".

**Why that is wrong:** The **Company** is the employer. The liability and the related on-costs stay in the Company after Completion. On-costs include:
- PAYG withholding;
- superannuation, depending on the character of the bonus;
- NSW payroll tax;
- workers' compensation premium.

Retention conditions also mean some amounts may fall due after Completion, when we own the Company.

**Push back:**
- Treat the full bonus pool **plus all on-costs** as Transaction Costs or Debt-like items, deducted from the price.
- Pay amounts falling due at Completion through Company payroll from the funds flow.
- For deferred or conditional amounts, deduct the maximum at Completion. Alternatively, hold them in escrow and release unused amounts to the Seller.
- Specific indemnity for any shortfall. Warranty that DD-005 lists all transaction-related bonuses, change-of-control payments and retention arrangements.

### 4.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)

**The facts:**
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**.
- DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open.
- There is no evidence of payment and no confirmatory assignment.

**Why the Seller's indemnity is too narrow:** Limiting it to the SOW3 payment covers only the AUD 180k. The real risk is that **the Company does not own IP that may be embedded in its product**. That could lead to infringement claims, injunctions, re-engineering costs and customer claims.

**Push back:**
- The Seller procures payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees before Completion, at the Seller's cost or deducted from the price.
- Delivery of a **signed confirmatory IP assignment and moral rights consent** from Ironquay is a condition precedent or Completion deliverable.
- If the assignment cannot be obtained, provide a broad specific indemnity covering:
  - third-party IP claims;
  - re-development or replacement costs;
  - customer losses;
  - injunction-related losses.
  
  This indemnity should sit outside the cap and basket, with a limitation period of at least 6 years.
- Confirm that the IP warranties are **not** "settled". They need to be specific, covering ownership of all product IP, contractor assignments and open-source compliance.

### 4.5 Export/privacy incident (DD-006, cl 4.6 / Sch 6)

**The facts:**
- A download link was sent to an unintended external address.
- About 1,240 records may be affected (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps).
- Access, scope and whether notification is needed are all unconfirmed.

**Why "not expected to be material" is unsupported:**
- With roughly AUD 12m turnover, the Company is very likely covered by the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).
- Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, a suspected eligible data breach must be assessed within **30 days** (s 26WH). If the incident occurred before 22 September, that window may already have passed. A late assessment is itself a compliance issue.
- Penalties and OAIC powers have increased following the 2022 and 2024 amendments.
- The incident may also breach customer contracts (data processing and confidentiality terms), including Bluefen's.

**Push back:**
- **Pre-Completion covenant:** the Seller completes the assessment promptly with qualified forensic support and shares the reports with the Buyer. Any notification to the OAIC or individuals is made if required, with Buyer input on wording.
- **Specific indemnity** covering:
  - regulatory penalties and investigation costs;
  - notification and remediation costs;
  - customer claims and credits;
  - third-party claims.
  
  It should sit outside the cap and basket and be unaffected by disclosure or knowledge.
- Expanded privacy and cyber warranties. Review cyber insurance cover and whether the insurer has been notified.

### 4.6 Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)

**The facts:**
- Three related renewals of AUD 110k each, totalling AUD 330k.
- The Seller calls them "ordinary course" but the disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.

**Why this needs scrutiny:** The Seller asks us to read the renewals "together for timing/scope". Three equal amounts suggest possible **contract splitting**. Each may sit just above or below an approval threshold.

**Push back:**
- Obtain the contracts, renewal dates and internal approvals.
- Check them against the conduct-of-business covenants and the Accounts date.
- Check whether Sandbar is a related party of the Seller.
- If the renewals were entered outside the ordinary course, were not budgeted, or are prepaid or committed spend with no matching value: treat them as Debt-like, deduct them from the price, or require their termination at the Seller's cost.
- Tighten pre-Completion covenants so that **aggregated** related commitments above AUD 50k–100k need Buyer consent.

### 4.7 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009): lower priority

The Seller says only a lease notification is needed and that a Mossvale consent is not triggered by a share sale. These are the Seller's characterisations.

**Action:**
- Have counsel review both clauses for deemed-assignment or change-in-control wording.
- Make the lease notification a Completion deliverable.
- Add a warranty that no material contract has change-of-control, termination or consent rights triggered by the transaction, other than those listed.

### 4.8 Tax

The Seller considers tax "settled under the general regime". That is not acceptable.

**Push back:**
- A **tax indemnity** (or tax deed) for all pre-Completion taxes, outside the cap and basket.
- Limitation period of at least the ATO amendment period plus a buffer, typically 5–7 years.
- Not subject to disclosure. Include conduct of tax claims provisions.

## 5. Security for recovery

There are several quantified exposures:
- Riverlark: AUD 3.2m
- Bonuses plus on-costs: about AUD 0.5m
- Ironquay: AUD 180k plus IP risk
- Sandbar: AUD 330k
- Privacy incident: unquantified
- Bluefen: revenue risk

Harbourglass is a vendor that may distribute the sale proceeds. We should consider:
- a **retention or escrow** (for example, 10–15% of the price for 18–24 months), and/or
- **W&I insurance**. This does not cover known issues, so the specific indemnities and price deductions above remain necessary.
